html:
SMTO-EXE-0236 — SMTO can't tell whether your Docker image was published

GUID: 43bc92d0-6c8a-51ba-a602-8e8b731918bf
Slug: docker-push-outcome-unknown
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • SMTO started sending your Docker image to the registry, but the upload broke off before it finished. The image might already be published, or it might not.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open your image registry's website (for example Docker Hub or your company registry) and find the image name and tag you were publishing. The registry is the only place that shows whether the upload actually finished.
  2. Check the tag's last-updated time. If it matches the time of this request, the image was published and you should not push it again. Pushing again could replace or duplicate an image that other people may already be using.
  3. Only if the tag is missing or still shows an older time, ask SMTO to push the image again, and approve the new request if SMTO asks. A new, separately approved push is the safe way to finish publishing when the first one didn't arrive.

What success looks like

  • The registry shows the image tag with an update time from your push, and SMTO's next push (if you needed one) reports success.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened in the registry before any new push. Then select Copy error details and send them, with the image name and tag, to the person who manages the registry or the Gateway. Don't keep asking SMTO to push the same image over and over.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An image push on the selected Gateway failed after the upload began, so the registry may or may not hold the new image; SMTO records the outcome as unknown and will not repeat the push.

What this means

  • An image push failed after the mutation boundary, so the service retained unknown registry-publication outcome rather than treating the push as unexecuted. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • An image push failed after the mutation boundary, so the service retained unknown registry-publication outcome rather than treating the push as unexecuted.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original push's exact repository/tag or digest and available registry/Engine evidence.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the target registry (web UI or registry API) for the pushed repository:tag and compare its digest and update time with the local image (docker.image). Only if the tag is absent or stale, issue a separately approved docker.image_push; never replay the original operation.
  • Inspect the selected Engine and registry state; do not replay an uncertain mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the selected Engine and registry state; do not replay an uncertain mutation.

How to verify the fix

  • Original publication is established before any separately authorized push.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
